cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword. (Controls: NES A: Swing the sword.)

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 rupees. It can be purchased for 60 Rupees behind a door reached from the Fairy Fountain area, and a shop in 2nd Quest sells it for 60 rupees.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need at least 5 Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items and Hyrule 3 documents. One Quest 1 walkthrough chunk says you need six heart containers to get it in that cave.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (obtained by going down the stairwell in the compass room area), as well as the Compass and two Keys earlier in the dungeon. The third Piece of Triforce and a Heart Container are also objectives of this dungeon.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4, making it the most powerful sword in the game and four times as powerful as the wooden sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers to receive it.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: The Raft allows Link to cross lakes and oceans, but it can only be used at a Dock; neither of the 'double docks' triggers raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. Fairies fill your hearts: a fairy enemy drop fills 3 of Link's hearts, and in the fairy ponds the fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: You can play the Money Making Game. In the Hyrule 1 documents, walking into the tree in section D-2 starts it, and in Hyrule 6 bombing the middle of the north wall in C-5 exposes a cave leading to it. Hyrule 2 also mentions a cave in A-5 where you can play it.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: At D-4 in Section 2 (2nd Quest), you can buy Arrows (the ability to use them) for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" when you start the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents describe the name "Zelda" but do not explicitly say whether the uppercase "ZELDA" triggers the same effect.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees in a shop reached from the Fairy Fountain: walk three screens south then two screens west, use a bomb near the notch to get 30 Rupees, return and heal, then walk south two and east four screens, bomb the rock wall for 30 Rupees, go one screen west and enter the door. The Blue Candle throws a flame that can light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but it can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. Strike him in the head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs those orbs; the regular shield lets them damage Link. Firing sword beams lets you hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
cases.answer: To enter Level 4 in the first quest, you need the Raft (listed as the prerequisite). Inside, the objectives include obtaining the Ladder, defeating the two-headed Gleeok, and obtaining the fourth Piece of Triforce, with a Heart Container also available.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The question is ambiguous since several dragon bosses exist. Aquamentus can be killed by two Bombs or by attacking it with the Sword or Arrows, but it can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon, must be defeated by stabbing each head until it flies free, then destroying every attached head, while dodging the flying heads' projectiles.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: Each Gleeok has one or more heads that must be stabbed until they fly freely around the room. A freed head is still a threat and cannot be defeated, so you must destroy every attached head to beat Gleeok. Defeating it earns a Heart Container.

cases.question: In the first quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: In the first quest, the Ladder is obtained in Dungeon 4, as its objectives list "Obtain the Ladder."

cases.question: In the second quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents don't say which dungeon in the second quest contains the Ladder. Dungeon 6 of Quest 2 lists "Obtain the Ladder" as an objective, which means the Ladder is found there. Dungeon 7 requires the Ladder as a prerequisite, so it is not the dungeon where it is found.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Swing the sword by pressing the A button. You can also use your selected subweapon with the B button.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack action in the game's controls.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your equipped subweapon, such as the Magical Wand, which fires magical blasts.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button on the NES controller to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map, change subweapon, and so on. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes, bombs can blast holes in weak walls. The item description says bombs can be used to kill enemies or blast holes in weak walls. Several walkthroughs also say to bomb walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your subweapon. Only the item in the blue box on the sub-screen can be assigned to B, and you change that assignment by switching to the sub-screen with Start.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also press B to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: You can heal by returning to a Fairy Fountain, where the fairy fills all your heart meters in the fairy ponds. You can also buy a Red Potion for 68 Rupees or a Water of Life for 40 Rupees from the medicine woman in the cave at D-4 on the 1st Quest map, if you have shown her the Letter. A Water of Life completely refills your life bar.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several places in the documents mention money: the Money Making Game is in a cave reached by bombing a rock face just left of the start screen (zelda1:cheats:004). In the 2nd Quest, you can burn the lower right tree in Hyrule 8 at B-2 for 10 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:002), or bomb the north wall of Hyrule 6 at C-5 to reach the Money Making Game (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-6:003). A Red Moblin in Hyrule 8 at B-4 (1st Quest) gives 30 Rupees after bombing the wall right of the crack (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:001).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: You can open a locked door in the first dungeon by leaving the room immediately and coming back, after which the locked door will open. Keys also open doors, with each key opening one door and Link able to carry up to nine until he obtains the magic key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Per the General Tips, if you're unsure how to proceed through a dungeon, bomb every wall that doesn't contain a door, since you'll typically find passageways leading further in. Passages to rooms in the "eyes" or unmarked rooms on the dungeon map are also often found this way.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is likely Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon boss. Link must attack each attached head; when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room, so dodge its projectiles and keep attacking the heads still attached to the body until every one is disconnected.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1's overworld, you get Bombs by defeating the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop them. The Quest 2 overworld list also includes getting some Bombs, and Quest 1 Dungeon 6 mentions replacement Bombs available from a woman two screens away.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is found in room O-1: enter the room with Traps in each corner, push aside the left-most block surrounded by blocks in the center to enter the stairwell, and you'll find the Bow. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding the bow.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save, choose "SAVE" with Select and press Start on the Game Over screen after dying; this stores your accomplishments until you next play. You can also quickly reach the Save Screen by pressing Up on the D-pad and A simultaneously on controller 2 from the sub-screen menu.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Heart Containers give Link an extra heart permanently. In Quest 1, burn the fifth tree from the right on the Lake Hylia coast screen (one screen north and one east of the shore) to find a fourth Heart Container, and bomb the lower-right corner of a huge rock on the foot of the eastern mountains to get the sixth. Fairies also refill hearts, but they only fill 3 hearts and don't add new ones.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in several shops, for example for 90 Rupees in a shop reached by burning a tree in Quest 1 (zelda1:overworld-quest-1:005), and for 90, 160, or 130 Rupees in various shops of the 2nd Quest overworld (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-2:002). The Magical Shield reflects more attacks than the Small Shield Link starts with (zelda1:items:026).

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Use a candle to light dark rooms: the Blue Candle can be used once per screen, and the Red Candle has no limit on uses per screen. Candles can light up dark rooms in dungeons.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air. The jump height is fixed, so tapping or holding A produces the same height.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve, and he can gain more by finding extra life items.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward a wall and cling to it, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it as you let go. Done correctly, you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating it can climb to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead, who moves at a slow, menacing pace and has a spinning weapon with good reach.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him. It uses no spirit points, but it replaces any weapon you currently hold and disappears after five seconds of use.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press B to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B to use your secondary weapon, which requires enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents mention ninpo techniques (Flame, Jump and Slash, Windmill Star) found in lamps and candles, but they do not explain how to get more ninpo or spirit points beyond collecting the red and blue Spirit Points tiles, which provide 10 and 5 points respectively. The documents say spirit points are needed to use secondary weapons, and that Jump and Slash drains them. They do not describe a specific method for gaining more ninpo, so I cannot fully answer that.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions you can collect: in Stage 4-2, a lamp on the left holds a potion that restores some lost health, and in Stage 3-1 a health-restoring potion sits over a small dock segment. Stage 2-2 also has an insect item containing a health-restoring potion, and in Stage 5-2 a candle above the first potion holds a health-restoring potion. Potions are found by destroying lamps, insects, and candles during stages.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: You were most likely sent back to 6-1 because you lost to one of the final bosses. The documents say that losing to any of them returns you to 6-1 regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, so you won't have to face them again.

cases.question: What is the password to skip to Act 5?
cases.answer: The documents do not contain a password to skip to Act 5. They state the opposite: you may not select or skip any level, and you must play every stage in order.
